summary: Every trial-shaped object this CLI marshals must always carry its phase key — empty when the registry posts no phase — and empty must never be rewritten to "NA".
reason: The generated structs tagged phase omitempty, so the key vanished from exactly the observational rows and consumers parsing the JSON in Python or R hit a KeyError on some rows and not others; the key has to be structurally present for a row to be parseable without per-row guards. Empty stays empty because the registry's own vocabulary distinguishes the two: "NA" is an interventional trial with no phase, an unposted phase is an observational study, and substituting one for the other asserts a study design the record does not claim. Trial.Phases is the list half of the same contract and marshals as [] rather than null so a consumer can iterate it unconditionally. Follow-up: the contract first landed on Trial and then extended to the three sibling structs that copy Trial.Phase verbatim — digestTrial, similarMatch, enrollmentVerdict. Deliberately outside it: fhirResearchStudy.Phase, where FHIR cardinality 0..1 makes a null an invalid resource, and the phase_distribution tallies in compare, emerging and recruiting, where an empty map means no distribution was computed rather than no phase posted. Guarded by TestPhaseKeyAlwaysPresentInJSON and TestTrialPhasesKeyAlwaysPresentInJSON.
validated_outcome: Re-adding omitempty to each of the four phase tags in turn, and to Trial.Phases, fails the corresponding subtest; a live digest measured 4 of 20 rows and similar 2 of 10 matches gaining the key, all with an empty value.
